title: Four AM field playbook — quick on-call crib
content:
Purpose:
A very small, portable crib for the 4am relief / bridge handoff. Not a canonical runbook — this is what I keep in my pocket when I take the shift: commands I actually use, gotchas I hit in the last week, and temporary shortcuts while we triage long-term fixes.

Top-of-shift checklist (first 5–10 min):
- Read last 30m channel history in #oncall and #prod-alerts (skim for paging loops or repeated 503s).
- Check PagerDuty: acknowledge any unacked incidents, note escalation owners.
- Quick health queries:
  - prom: sum(rate(redwood_http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) by (route) -> spike audit
  - prom: increase(gpu_queue_length[5m]) -> backlog alert
  - kibana: recent 5xx for /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings (filter by model id)
- Console: look at per-route latency dashboard -> sort by p95, check for routes > SLO
- Confirm dedicated pools status: `rdctl pools list` (should be green)

Common quick fixes (what I actually run):
- Router flaps / 503s: restart ingress proxy on node with high conn count:
  - `kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deploy/ingress-proxy` (watch logs `kubectl logs -f`)
- Stuck batcher (queue growing but GPUs idle): restart batcher deployment and bump batch_window to 20ms temporary:
  - `kubectl -n serving set env deploy/batcher BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/batcher`
- KV cache pressure: evict oldest 10% via admin endpoint -> `curl -X POST https://svc-admin/cache/evict?percent=10` (auth: service token in vault)
- Model variant fallback misroute: toggle routing policy to fallback-tier:
  - `rdctl routing set-policy --name emergency-fallback --priority=high`

Known issues / sticky notes (recent):
- INF-4123: intermittent latency regression on long-seq (>2048) requests when using quantized-8bit kernel. Temporary mitigation: pin clients to float16 model variant for heavy long-context jobs. See linked artifact.
- Autoscaler thrash at 02:00 PST: scan shows violent scale up/down due to bursty eval jobs. Workaround: set min_replicas=2 on dedicated pools for the night window.
- Cache key collision pattern observed for chat sessions with non-ASCII metadata; I added a quick pre-escape in the router but need proper fix (PR referenced).

Escalation ladder (who to call text/voice):
- Pager: first -> oncall_primary (PD)
- If PD fails or incident >sev2: call Jamie Ortiz (eng infra lead) mobile +1 (415) 555-0192
- Hardware/GPU smoke: call DataCenterOps -> slack @dc-ops and seatbelt pager (internal)
- Legal / Data privacy smell: call security-signal channel and page Security (Anika Bose)

Short-term config changes I sometimes make (document them in ticket):
- Bump request timeout for heavy embeddings route to 180s in route config (temporary).
- Set model fallback multiplier to 1.5 during sustained load (>80% GPU util).
- Add temporary traffic-shed rule: 429 for anonymous keys when global qps > threshold (put exact rule in INF ticket).

Observability quick hits (links/queries I paste into Slack):
- p95 latency (last 15m): `sum(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[15m])) by (le, route)))`
- GPU util by pool: `avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[10m]) by (pool)`
- Error spike timeline: `sum(increase(redwood_errors_total[1m])) by (error_type)` -> heatmap in console

Open questions / to follow up:
- Who owns the router pre-escape for non-ASCII metadata? (Left a note in INF-4209; need owner for a proper test).
- Longer-term: should we surface a per-customer soft-QPS so platform owners can triage noisy tenants without global shed?

Backfill notes for morning handoff (what to tell next shift):
- If you restart batcher, monitor GPU utilization for 5–10m; if it stays low while queue climbs, re-open INF-4123 and escalate to applied-ml.
- Any temporary env changes I made are tagged `four-am-temp-<date>` in infra config; revert after 48h unless ticket attached.
- I leave the scratch auth token in vault path `secret/oncall/fouram` (rotate after using).

Pocket log (recent quick entries):
- 2026-02-11 04:12: restarted ingress-proxy on node gke-prod-3 due to too-many-conns -> p95 dropped from 1.8s to 0.45s
- 2026-02-12 03:51 bumped BATCH_WINDOW_MS to 20ms while investigating stuck batches; left note in PR #982

Notes to self (todo):
- Convert the handy `rdctl` commands into a small script under `scripts/oncall/` so bridging handoffs are less command-y.
- Add a tiny checklist card in Confluence with the top 5 queries for 4am shift.
- Reproduce the non-ASCII cache key locally and add unit test.

If you pick this up mid-incident: keep the channel focused. One person types, one person runs commands, document every change (exact command + timestamp).

End of crib. Keep this ephemeral. If something becomes recurring, promote to shared runbook under eng-sre > runbooks.
